sources.about: Injections planted in real web pages a browsing agent reads (same-origin and cross-origin, inbound and outbound).
Agentic injections (prompt extraction, role-play, tool abuse, authority claims) each paired with a benign twin on the same topic.
Agentic injection techniques with labelled families, and hard negatives (questions about attacks, legitimate role-play).
Poisoned MCP tool descriptions (override, exfiltration, stealth) with the clean description of the same tool.
Japanese documents (email, news, minutes) with an injected instruction, as a reading tool returns them.
Injections in repository files (README, config, PR templates) that steer a code-review agent; the dataset's [FILETYPE=]/[ATTACK=] tags removed.
Prompts that try to extract an agent's system prompt and secrets (direct asking, role-play, gradual extraction, encoding).
Jailbreak prompts collected from Discord, Reddit and prompt sites (Shen et al., CCS 2024); the regular prompts from the same communities as benign.
Text jailbreak templates, persuasion and logic attacks (image-only formats excluded).
Labelled injections across categories, with security-adjacent hard negatives (research-licensed WildGuard rows and HarmBench goals left out).
Labelled injections and benign prompts.
Injections by category (format-string, encoding, override) and benign prompts.
Subtle injections (misdirection, output manipulation, instruction hijacking inside a plausible task).
Injections in several languages.
Jailbreak prompts (output-format constraints, refusal suppression, prefix forcing).
Injections by category (override, leakage, role play) and benign prompts.
Paraphrased overrides and soft reframes, with hard negatives that use the same trigger words.
Tool outputs (email, documents, pages) carrying an injection in an agent flow.
Meta CyberSecEval 3 prompt-injection test inputs (direct and indirect variants, machine-translated set included).
JailbreakBench submitted jailbreaks (PAIR, random search, jailbreakchat templates, GCG transfer).
PyRIT jailbreak templates (persona, developer mode, refusal suppression), placeholder filled with a system-prompt request.
User turns that try to pull a system-prompted chatbot out of its role (persona swaps, scope breaks), with the in-scope turns as benign.
Injections labelled by family and technique (delimiter injection, authority impersonation, prompt extraction), with hard negatives about those techniques.
Short prompt-extraction and protocol-bypass requests in several European languages.
Hand-written injections by category (instruction override, role-play, extraction, encoding) and benign prompts.
Agent-security test inputs by category (injection, jailbreak, exfiltration, tool abuse, multi-agent), with over-refusal prompts as benign.
Turkish customer-service conversations with injected turns, each paired with the benign turn.
Turkish injections by family and technique (acrostic leaks, role-play, override), with hard negatives.
A catalogue of injection payloads by technique and language, each mapped to OWASP and ATLAS.
The same catalogue written in Turkish.
Injections and benign prompts for a classifier, including placeholder-secret extraction.
Injections that try to make a crypto-wallet agent transfer funds or reveal keys, with benign wallet requests.
Injections labelled by type (role confusion, developer-mode claims, extraction), with benign prompts.
Injections that claim a sandbox, test mode or new authority, with benign prompts.
Each injection mirrored by a benign prompt on the same topic and category (persona, extraction, override).
Machine-written direct and indirect injections with benign prompts.
Injections by attack type with benign prompts.
Vietnamese and code-switched Vietnamese/English injections with benign prompts.
Injections (mostly German) each with two safe rewrites, the rewrites as benign.
TrustLLM jailbreak triggers by technique (refusal-sentence prohibition, fixed opening, leetspeak, JSON format, CoT).
StrongREJECT jailbreak templates translated into Greek.
Guardrail evaluation inputs: persona overrides and instruction-format jailbreaks to block, ordinary requests to allow.
Role-play jailbreaks that push a model to write panic-inducing posts.
Jailbreak wrappers by name (prefix injection, refusal suppression, combinations), one row per wrapper.
Adversarial rewrites of a request by strategy (typos, output encoding, role-play), written in a generated persona.
A system prompt and user request with an injection embedded in the user content ([SYSTEM OVERRIDE], "Actual instruction:").
Injections by category (system impersonation, override, exfiltration) with clean factual sentences.
Hand-written injections by category, including agent exfiltration through tool URLs.
Benign only: Hugging Face documentation on writing and applying chat templates, in pieces as a fetch tool returns them.
Benign only: the Jinja chat and tool-calling templates vLLM ships, as a file-read tool returns them.
Benign only: a collection of chat templates for open models (ChatML, Llama 2 and 3, Gemma, Mistral, Phi) and its README.
Benign only: llama.cpp documentation on function calling and the server, including chat-template formats.
Benign only: everyday requests by task type and domain, written as negatives for an injection classifier.
